The late economist Daniel Kahneman won a Nobel Prize for demonstrating what
every sports champion knows: losing hurts twice as badly as winning feels
good.

The Democratic triumph last week was gigantic enough to challenge that
formula. They smothered Donald Trump's MAGA movement, won fat House and Senate
majorities, and scored breakthrough victories that re-shuffle the presidential
map. The glow from resuscitating the American experiment will last awhile.

But the calendar is already presenting their next set of challenges. The
incoming Congress, juggling calls for addressing Americans' affordability
problems and pursuing accountability for Trump's depredations, has to set
priorities for the next two years.

Left and center-left factions have begun wrestling over their competing
visions of the Democratic Party's 21st century identity. The near-term balance
between ambition and pragmatism will turn on the just-getting-started race for
the 2028 presidential nomination.

Trump has sent wildly divergent signals about his plans for the remaining time
America is stuck with him.
